value: Mass, length, time, temperature (Y, W, U, V)
reasoning: Fundamental quantities do not depend on other quantities. Mass, length, time and temperature are fundamental. Weight (mass times g) and momentum (mass times velocity) are derived, so every option with X or Z is wrong.

1 is true: a charged object attracts a neutral one by induction. 2 is false: gaining electrons makes an atom negative. 3 is true: charge is never created, only transferred from one body to another. 4 is true: losing electrons leaves an atom positive.

runnerUp: B, if the setup is read as measuring the block's acceleration to test Newton's second law
reasoning: When enough load is hung, the pull of the thread (a force) moves the block along the table, and the scale beside the block measures how far it moves (the displacement). Knowing the force and the displacement lets us verify that work done is \(W = Fs\).

Pressure is force divided by area, \(P = \frac{F}{A}\). The weight is the same in every position, so pressure is least when the area touching the ground is largest, which happens when the person lies on the back.
Work, energy and heat are all forms of energy and are measured in joules. Specific heat is measured in J/kg°C (joule per kilogram per degree), not in joules.

value: Density of liquid and volume of the object (1, 2)
reasoning: Buoyant force equals the weight of liquid displaced: \(F = V\rho g\), where \(V\) is the volume of the object immersed and \(\rho\) is the density of the liquid. The amount of liquid in the vessel, the object's own density and the depth do not change it.
Water freezes at 0 °C. In Fahrenheit that is \(\frac{9}{5}\times 0 + 32 = 32\) °F, and in kelvin it is \(0 + 273 = 273\) K.

value: Volume decreases and pressure decreases (Y, W)
reasoning: Cooling the sealed air makes its molecules move slower, so the pressure of the air falls; the cold metal bottle also contracts slightly. Every other option says the pressure increases, which cannot happen on cooling, so Y and W is the correct choice.

P lies on the bisector, so it makes \(60^\circ\) with each mirror and is \(4\sin 60^\circ = 2\sqrt{3}\) cm from each mirror. Each image is twice that, \(4\sqrt{3}\) cm, from P. The images and P are all 4 cm from the meeting point and \(120^\circ\) apart, so the triangle is equilateral with side \(4\sqrt{3}\) cm and perimeter \(12\sqrt{3}\) cm.

One round is \(2\pi r = 2\times\frac{22}{7}\times 70 = 440\) m, so speed is \(\frac{440}{44} = 10\) m/s. He comes back to the starting point, so his displacement is zero and his average velocity is 0 m/s.

value: d = 875 m, v = 35 m/s, a = 2 m/s²
reasoning: From the graph, velocity is 10 m/s at 5 s and 60 m/s at 30 s. Acceleration \(a = \frac{60-10}{30-5} = \frac{50}{25} = 2\ \mathrm{m/s^2}\). Average velocity \(= \frac{10+60}{2} = 35\) m/s, so distance \(= 35\times 25 = 875\) m.

value: P potential, Q kinetic, R kinetic, S light energy
runnerUp: D, if P is taken as a boiler holding heat energy and the bulb at S is described by the electrical energy reaching it
reasoning: P is a closed container of compressed steam, which stores energy because of its compressed state (potential energy). At Q the steam rushes out as a jet (kinetic energy) and turns the turbine wheel R (kinetic energy of rotation). The generator drives the bulb at S, which gives out light energy. The item depends on how P and S are read, so the figure leaves room for doubt.

value: Power: g cm² s⁻³ and kg m² s⁻³
reasoning: Power is work per second: \(\mathrm{kg\,m^2 s^{-2}}\) divided by s gives \(\mathrm{kg\,m^2 s^{-3}}\), and in CGS \(\mathrm{g\,cm^2 s^{-3}}\). The force and work options have the wrong power of s, and the units in D belong to force, not pressure.

In parallel every appliance gets the same potential difference (2), so each works at its rated capacity (1), and if one stops working the others still run (4). Statement 3 is false: the current through each appliance depends on its own resistance, so it is not the same.

value: Different wavelengths and different refractive indices
reasoning: White light is made of colours of different wavelengths. Water drops have a different refractive index for each wavelength, so each colour bends by a different amount and the colours spread out into a rainbow.

value: Only the pole (R) is not common
runnerUp: B, if the focal length is treated as different because one piece is concave and another convex (opposite signs)
reasoning: Pieces cut from the same sphere have the same radius of curvature, so the same focal length (half the radius), and their centre of curvature is the centre of that sphere. The pole is the middle point of each mirror's own surface, so it is different for each mirror.
Watt, horse power and N m s⁻¹ (joule per second) are all units of power. \(\mathrm{N\,m^{-2}}\) is force per area, a unit of pressure, so it is the odd one out.

value: P = ammeter, Q = key, R = voltmeter, S = resistor
runnerUp: D, which swaps R and S; since R and S are both in the parallel pair, a voltmeter across a resistor is equally correct either way round, so the item may have two right answers
reasoning: P and Q are in the main line with the cell, so they take the ammeter (2) and the key (4), both of which go in series. R and S are joined in parallel, so they take the resistor and the voltmeter, which must be connected across the resistor. S lies on the main wire, so it carries the resistor (1), and R is the loop drawn around it for the voltmeter (3). Options A and C put the voltmeter in series, which is wrong.

In a gas, \(v \propto \sqrt{\frac{T}{M}}\). So 4 is true and 1 is false (speed rises with temperature, it is not inversely proportional). 2 is true. 3 is false: at a fixed temperature, changing the pressure does not change the speed of sound.
The boy is 165 m from wall A and \(495 - 165 = 330\) m from wall B. Echo from A: \(\frac{2\times165}{330} = 1\) s. Echo from B: \(\frac{2\times330}{330} = 2\) s. The difference is \(2 - 1 = 1\) s.
When the kinetic energy becomes half, 490 J has turned into potential energy. \(mgh = 490\), so \(h = \frac{490}{2\times 9.8} = 25\) m.
\(p = mv\) is constant, so \(v = \frac{p}{m}\): velocity is inversely proportional to mass. The graph is a curve that falls steeply and then flattens, never touching either axis, which is Figure (A).
Acceleration \(a = \frac{F}{m} = \frac{100}{2} = 50\ \mathrm{m/s^2}\). Change in velocity \(= at = 50\times 10 = 500\) m/s.

During free fall the speed increases, so momentum and kinetic energy increase, while the height falls, so potential energy decreases. The mass stays the same, and the total mechanical energy stays constant because potential energy is turned into kinetic energy.

value: All four statements P, Q, R, S are correct
reasoning: Work by the coolie \(= mgh = 80\times 9.8\times 5 = 3920\) J, positive because his force and the motion are both upward (Q, S true). Gravity acts downward against the upward motion, so its work is negative (P true). Power \(= \frac{3920}{4} = 980\) J/s (R true).

value: Copper, aluminium, platinum, nichrome (z, x, y, w)
reasoning: Copper has the lowest resistivity (about \(1.7\times10^{-8}\ \Omega\,m\)), then aluminium (about \(2.7\times10^{-8}\)), then platinum (about \(10.6\times10^{-8}\)). Nichrome, an alloy, is far higher (about \(1.1\times10^{-6}\)).
CD, DVD and pen drive are secondary storage devices that keep data after the power is off. RAM is the computer's primary (main) memory and loses its data when the power is switched off.
Total time \(= 20\times 5 = 100\) h. Power \(= \frac{2.5\ \mathrm{kWh}}{100\ \mathrm{h}} = 0.025\) kW \(= 25\) W.

value: Image is virtual and magnified (X, W)
reasoning: A concave mirror gives an erect image only when the object is between the pole and the focus. That image is virtual (X true), so it cannot be taken on a screen (Y false), and it is enlarged, so the magnification is more than +1 (W true, Z false).

runnerUp: A, if the analogy is read as recovering pure water from muddy water by distillation
reasoning: Kerosene and water do not mix, so they are separated by a physical method (a separating funnel). Muddy water has fine insoluble clay particles suspended in it, and these are separated by spinning the mixture fast, which is centrifugation. Distillation and chromatography are used for dissolved substances.

value: Lime, silica, alumina, iron oxide, gypsum
runnerUp: C, if magnesia is counted as a listed ingredient instead of gypsum
reasoning: Portland cement is made by heating lime and clay (which supplies silica, alumina and iron oxide), and gypsum is added to the clinker to slow down setting. So its ingredients are lime, silica, alumina, iron oxide and gypsum. Option A lists concrete, not cement.
Hematite, limonite and siderite are ores of iron. Bauxite is the ore of aluminium, so it is the odd one out.
A low-pressure sodium vapour lamp contains sodium with a small amount of neon and argon gas. These gases start the discharge and warm the lamp until the sodium vaporises.

value: Potassium ferrocyanide, platinum nitrate, chlorophyll, vitamin B-12
runnerUp: D, if 'complex compounds' is read as large biological molecules rather than metal complexes
reasoning: A complex compound has a metal atom bonded to a group of surrounding atoms or ions. Potassium ferrocyanide has iron, chlorophyll has magnesium and vitamin B-12 has cobalt at its centre. Common salt, urea, carbohydrates and proteins are not metal complexes, so every other option contains a wrong member.
Galvanizing (zinc coating), tinning (tin coating), anodizing (a protective oxide layer on aluminium) and alloying (as in stainless steel) all protect metals from corrosion.

Magnesium hydroxide (milk of magnesia) is a mild base that neutralises extra acid in the stomach, so it is used as an antacid. Potassium hydroxide and calcium hydroxide are too strong and harmful to swallow.

I is right: an acid reacts with a base (sodium bicarbonate) to form a salt, a neutralization reaction. II is right: citrate is \(\mathrm{C_6H_5O_7^{3-}}\), so sodium citrate is \(\mathrm{Na_3C_6H_5O_7}\). III is wrong: sodium citrate dissolves in water. IV is right: sodium bicarbonate is sodium hydrogen carbonate.

runnerUp: A, if copper oxide's blue colour is taken as the bluish green
reasoning: Iron(II) oxide (ferrous oxide) gives glass a bluish green colour, as seen in many bottles. Copper oxide gives a peacock blue colour, while calcium oxide adds no colour.
In \(\mathrm{CO_2}\), carbon is 12 and oxygen is \(2\times16 = 32\), so the ratio is \(12:32 = 3:8\). Sulphur dioxide is \(32:32 = 1:1\) and magnesium oxide is \(24:16 = 3:2\).

Molecular masses: \(\mathrm{H_2O} = 18\), \(\mathrm{NaOH} = 23+16+1 = 40\), \(\mathrm{CO_2} = 12+32 = 44\), \(\mathrm{MgCl_2} = 24+71 = 95\). In ascending order: \(\mathrm{H_2O}\), NaOH, \(\mathrm{CO_2}\), \(\mathrm{MgCl_2}\).
Sodium phosphate is \(\mathrm{Na_3PO_4}\). Sodium forms \(\mathrm{Na^+}\) and the phosphate radical carries a charge of 3 minus, \(\mathrm{PO_4^{3-}}\), which is why three sodium ions are needed.

Carbon dioxide turns to gas at about \(-78\) °C, oxygen boils at about \(-183\) °C, argon at about \(-186\) °C and nitrogen at about \(-196\) °C. From highest to lowest: \(\mathrm{CO_2}\), \(\mathrm{O_2}\), Ar, \(\mathrm{N_2}\).
Bromine has atomic number 35, so a neutral atom has 35 electrons. The \(\mathrm{Br^-}\) ion has gained one electron, giving 36.

value: (NH₄)₂SO₄, basic radical NH₄⁺, acidic salt, fertilizer
reasoning: Ammonium is \(\mathrm{NH_4^+}\) and sulphate is \(\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}}\), so the formula is \(\mathrm{(NH_4)_2SO_4}\) and the basic radical is \(\mathrm{NH_4^+}\). It comes from a strong acid and a weak base, so it is an acidic salt, and it is used as a nitrogen fertilizer for soil.
Sulphuric acid, sodium hydroxide and potassium hydroxide dissociate almost completely in water (strong). Formic acid, HCOOH, dissociates only partly, so it is a weak acid and the odd one out.
Molar mass of NaOH \(= 23+16+1 = 40\) g/mol, so 60 g is \(\frac{60}{40} = 1.5\) mol. Molarity \(= \frac{1.5\ \mathrm{mol}}{2\ \mathrm{L}} = 0.75\) M.

value: Sulphamic acid, boric acid, oxalic acid (II, III, V)
reasoning: Sulphamic acid, boric acid and oxalic acid are crystalline solids at room temperature. Carbonic acid exists only in solution (carbon dioxide in water), and hydrochloric acid is a solution of hydrogen chloride gas.

I is true: each side has 1 Ca, 2 N, 8 O and 4 H, so the equation is balanced. II is false: \(\mathrm{Ca(NO_3)_2}\) comes from a strong acid and a strong base, so it is a neutral salt. III is true: a neutral salt solution has pH 7. IV is not right as stated: \(\mathrm{Ca(OH)_2}\) is slaked lime, while lime (quicklime) is CaO.
Sulphur (rhombic, monoclinic), phosphorus (white, red) and carbon (diamond, graphite) all show allotropy. Chlorine does not have allotropes, so it is the odd one out.
